correctness.rationale: The 36-vertex cubic graph has exactly 21 hexagons: 18 outer/spoke cycles and 3 inner six-cycles; exhaustive enumeration proves 42 maximal exceptional radius-two triangles and the face vector (36,162,186,36). The centered subcomplex simplicially collapses to the graph in 144 verified free-face pairs. Homotopy invariance of CW attachment replaces the 42 exceptional triangles with two disks per hexagon: the 21 second disks split off 21 integral two-spheres. The first 18 outer hexagon disks pair with their private inner edges, reducing the graph to its outer circle; each of the three inner loops then winds once around that circle, the first kills it and the other two give two additional spheres. Thus the exact integral homotopy type is a wedge of 23 S^2, with pi_1=1 and no torsion. A second exact cellular reduction performs 127 legal two-cell generator eliminations and leaves 23 null attaching words, confirming the topological claim; exact boundary ranks over F2,F3,F5 are auxiliary only. Scope is one exact finite graph, with no unproved infinite extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The stable same-family theorem starts at n=19 and expressly excludes n=18. The general hexagon-packing theorem assumes all distinct six-cycles are edge-disjoint; every outer edge here lies on three distinct hexagons. Adamaszek’s radius-two collapse requires girth at least seven or absence of exceptional triangles; the present graph has girth six and 42 such triangles. Metric gluing results impose a decomposable short-path configuration not provided by these mutually overlapping cycles. Other GP(n,2) results concern different graph families.

originality.rationale: The closest published same-graph-family theorem proves a stable n>=19 integral wedge and explicitly gives only mod-two homology at the exceptional n=18, without asserting integral homotopy. The new proof identifies the three additional inner hexagons as circle-killing degree-one attaching maps and establishes integral homotopy equivalence at n=18. Existing general hexagon-packing results require edge-disjoint six-cycles, which fails because GP(18,3) has overlapping outer-spoke hexagons. General clique-graph-power, gluing and hypercube Rips theorems do not cover this exact case.

value.rationale: The stable n>=19 classification expressly identifies the excluded n=18 case and provides only mod-two ranks there. The new integral homotopy classification determines simply connectivity, torsion-freeness and an explicit 23-sphere wedge, identifies 21 local hexagon spheres and two extra sphere classes, and explains why the three inner hexagons kill the stable-range circle. This exact natural boundary answers a genuinely motivated missing topology question; it is not just recomputing the known mod-two vector, a generic small-parameter substitution or an unsupported extension to arbitrary n.
